title: WAG reply (wag-protocol/2)
description: The JSON object that ends a player's reply to a WAG prompt. Only `action` is required. A bare move object (protocol 1) is also accepted; see `#/$defs/action`. The server accepts some other spellings of the field names (docs/protocol.md); this schema gives the canonical ones.

context.description: What the player observes on the board that matters for this move: one observation per item.

thoughts.description: The player's reasoning, step by step: one step per item. A stated rationale, not a faithful record of how the move was chosen.

summary.description: One or two sentences: the situation, the reasoning and the move.

expect.description: Labels the player predicts for some statements after the move. The server checks them (trace field expect_check).

stmt.description: A statement reference ("s3"), a statement ID, or "claim".

alternatives.description: Moves the player considered and did not make. The server tries up to three of them on the game and undoes them (trace field alternative_outcomes).

confidence.description: How likely, from 0 to 1, the player thinks the move helps its side.

type.description: support: a new argument (no target), a defence (target_arg_id and answers_cq_id), or an argument for a statement (target_stmt_id). attack: a negative answer to a critical question, or an argument against a statement. question: a critical question or a challenge, asked without an argument. abstain: pass. resign.

scheme_id.description: The scheme of the argument, e.g. AS:position_to_know (not for a question).

target_arg_id.description: The argument a critical question is about, e.g. a1.

answers_cq_id.description: The critical question answered or asked, e.g. CQ:possibility; CQ:premise_acceptable is the challenge of a premise.

target_premise_id.description: The premise the question is about, when the prompt lists one: a reference (s3) or a statement ID.

target_stmt_id.description: The statement a support argues for, or an attack argues against: a reference (s3) or a statement ID. A move with it names no argument, premise or question.

variable_bindings.description: The scheme's parts as short phrases, by variable name. Leave out the answer part and the parts the statement fixes.

text.description: The argument in the player's own words.
